### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**12** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 098481744fd7dd9d0eade7cb61701891c5a890cb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `17d7d90d78a0651abe3682c3044ec0bdcfb1ee01` — the merge of head `5a4e282ffbf19ed71611c58abacfd9a79281d35f` into base `098481744fd7dd9d0eade7cb61701891c5a890cb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 17d7d90d78a0651abe3682c3044ec0bdcfb1ee01 && git checkout 17d7d90d78a0651abe3682c3044ec0bdcfb1ee01
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 098481744fd7dd9d0eade7cb61701891c5a890cb 5a4e282ffbf19ed71611c58abacfd9a79281d35f && git checkout -B drift-repro 098481744fd7dd9d0eade7cb61701891c5a890cb && git merge --no-ff 5a4e282ffbf19ed71611c58abacfd9a79281d35f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 098481744fd7dd9d0eade7cb61701891c5a890cb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5a4e282ffbf19ed71611c58abacfd9a79281d35f`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #22787 (body, claim `6106434946`, report `6107295475`), ADR-0139 at `origin/main` (D1–D6, Execution plan), #22788, PR #22809 (body, 11 files, +699/−4, `git diff origin/main...5a4e282ffb`), the head's `engine.ts`, both `filter-comparand-shape.ts`, `filter-subtree-provenance.ts`, `activity-read-visibility.ts`, `parent-record-read-gate.ts#andIntoWhere`, `filter.zod.ts#parseFilterAST`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs`, `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`, `.changeset/config.json`, `.github/workflows/{ci,lint}.yml`, and the check-runs on the head. Judged as a read-authorization change.

### ① Derived judgments

**D1 (a), no request can spell it — RIGHT.**
- No operator added: `filter.zod.ts` is not in the file list; `FieldOperatorsSchema` and `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` are unchanged at the head; the schema doors refuse `{ $in: leaf }` (spec pin).
- No ingress produces a value `isReadableIds` accepts: the brand is an own `Symbol.for` key, non-enumerable, non-writable, non-configurable, on a frozen object, defined exactly as `markFilterSubtreeProvenance` defines its mark (`filter-subtree-provenance.ts:176-180`). REST body, query string, the RPC and Virtual Data Engine wires, stored metadata and a flow or formula filter all arrive through JSON or a structured clone, which drop symbol keys; `isReadableIds` also demands the value `true` and a non-empty string `object`, so a forged string key or a prototype-inherited brand answers false (spec pins: json, structuredClone, spread, Object.assign, inherited, array, wrong value).
- In-process construction through the exported `ReadableIds.of` (or a hand-made `Symbol.for` property, which the spec test itself does) is possible by design, exactly as the provenance mark is: the brand separates "built in this process" from "crossed a wire", not trusted from untrusted modules. It is not an escalation route: the leaf carries only an object name and no grant; today the engine refuses it 500 before any driver resolves (objectql pins, zero driver calls), and a direct driver call bypassing the engine answers a raw TypeError (memory), `500 DATABASE_ERROR` (sql) or an unchanged non-array `$in` (mongodb), none of which widens (dev measurement at `a2e94c2a05`; not re-run here). What E2 must keep true: the composed form is derived ONLY from the reading caller's `canReadObject` and `getReadFilter` on `leaf.object` under the request's own context, so a constructed leaf can never resolve to more than that caller could read of P directly; the uncomposed leaf (no `scope`) stays refused at the engine AND, after E3 and E4, at every driver as D2's "never evaluated as no restriction"; a system-context read composing a leaf is decided explicitly, never by falling through.

**D1 (b), losing the brand fails closed — RIGHT.** The spec door's `$in` branch (`filter-comparand-shape.ts:1088-1090`) admits only `op === '$in' && admitReadableIds && isReadableIds(comparand)` and otherwise throws `nonListComparandError`; nothing drops the `$in`. Pins exist for JSON (spec and objectql), a structured clone (both), a spread (both) and `Object.assign` (spec), all refused `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 even with the option set, with zero driver calls on the engine side.

**D1 (c), it is a leaf — RIGHT, one pin gap flagged in ③.** Admission is at `$in` alone; `$nin` shares the branch and is refused with the option (spec pin). `$between` is judged before the admission, so a leaf endpoint passes the shape door and meets the engine refusal (objectql pin `where.amount.$between[1]`). `having` and `aggregations[i].filter` reach the objectql wrapper (`engine.ts:19049`, `:18912`) and so the refusal; the aggregation filter is pinned, `having` is not. Write verbs: `update` and `delete` call the same door (`engine.ts:15188`, `:18165`) and are pinned at 500 with `multi: true`. Implicit equality, `$eq`, a list member and a nested-relation condition are pinned at 500.

**The opt-in route — RIGHT.** At the head the spec function is the rule's only implementation: objectql's `assertListComparandShapes` delegates and adds the `find('x')` prefix (`packages/objectql/src/filter-comparand-shape.ts:119`). Every other caller passes no option and keeps refusing the leaf as a non-list, verified by name: `filter.zod.ts:2825` (`parseFilterAST`), `filter-save-door-refusals.ts:131` (the save door), `service-analytics/src/strategies/filter-normalizer.ts:1689,1691,1771` and `read-scope-sql.ts:1078` (analytics), `plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts:378`, `lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts:910`, `driver-memory/src/memory-analytics.ts:1824`. Placing a universal admission in the shared function, or the admission in objectql's wrapper, would either let `parseFilterAST` and memory analytics pass a leaf to a driver or fork the rule into two implementations; the opt-in in the one implementation is the correct home. `ListComparandShapeOptions` as a public interface is acceptable: `assertListComparandShapes` is already a published spec export, so its parameter type must be published for the declaration to build, and the docblock names the one caller that may pass it. It is an engine-internal knob on the authoring contract, but one that admits nothing on its own: a third-party caller that passes it still hands the leaf to the engine's door (500) or to a driver that refuses or errors; after E3 the drivers must keep refusing the uncomposed form so the option can never become a bypass.

**The fail-closed window, E1 to E2 — RIGHT.** 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` is the right code: no request can spell the leaf, so the fault is in-process code, and the envelope is the one ADR-0139 D3 gives a driver's own refusal (status 500, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, message naming the leaf, its position and the remedy); `packages/rest/src/error-response.ts:244,338` withholds 5xx prose from the wire and logs it. Coverage at the head: `find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate` (`where`, `aggregations[i].filter`, `having`), `update` and `delete` all pass `lowerWhereFilterArray`'s object branch into the wrapper before `getDriver` or any driver call; `count`'s no-`driver.count` fallback re-enters `find`; the engine's internal `driver.find` calls (`resolveSecretField`, `resolveInternalField`, the update and delete pre-reads) take engine-built wheres, not caller filters. Paths that skip the objectql binding are exactly the two the dev reported (next two items) plus a plugin holding a driver reference directly, which is outside the engine by construction and is what D2's driver-side refusal exists for.

**Dev out-of-scope finding 1 — VERIFIED, ESCALATED to E2 (#22788), not a PASS condition.** At the head, `find` runs `lowerWhereFilterArray` (the door), then `resolveWhereTokens` (`engine.ts:12920`), whose `resolveRelateThenLowerWhere` is where `lowerRelationConditions` runs (`:12509`, D2's named seam), and only then `executeWithMiddleware` (`:12922`); `installActivityReadVisibility` registers an object-scoped middleware (`activity-read-visibility.ts:128-147`) whose `andIntoWhere` assigns `ctx.ast.where` (`parent-record-read-gate.ts:157`), and inside the executor `triggerHooks('beforeFind')` runs on the same AST before `driver.find(object, hookContext.input.ast)` (`:12938`). So a leaf written by a D4 emitter, or by any `beforeFind` hook, meets neither the door nor D2's seam. No live exposure today: `computeParentRecordFilter` emits `$in` id lists from its pre-scan, and `git grep` at the head finds no `ReadableIds.of(` outside `readable-ids.ts`, its docblock mention in the spec door, and the two test files. E1's claim scoped `engine.ts` out of the surface, so stop-and-report was the right act. What E2 must do: compose once, on the FINAL AST, at the executor boundary between the `before*` hooks and the `driver.*` call for each read verb (after the middleware chain is not enough, because hooks run inside the executor), and move the uncomposed refusal to that same point so a consumer-emitted leaf that is not composed is refused rather than handed down; the alternative, making the D4 emitters write before the seam, contradicts the object-scoped middleware the six gates are installed through and should not be taken.

**Dev out-of-scope finding 2 — VERIFIED, ESCALATED to E2, same fix.** `lowerWhereFilterArray`'s array branch lowers through `parseFilterAST` (`engine.ts:1202`), which runs the spec door with no option, and the objectql wrapper is not called on the lowered condition (`:1215` records why the second call was deleted). Consequence: a `$in` leaf in the array form is refused 400 (spec pin), so no leaf passes the door there; a leaf at a non-`$in` position in the array form, e.g. the tuple `record_id = leaf`, lowers to implicit equality (`filter.zod.ts#convertComparison`), passes the shape door as a plain object with no `$` key, and reaches `resolveWhereTokens` and the driver without meeting `refuseUncomposedReadableIds`. Reach: in-process callers using the array sugar directly on the engine, none in-repo; an equality against an object matches nothing on any driver, so it does not widen. The position refusal does not cover that lowered condition; one seam at the executor boundary (finding 1) covers both branches, so E2 should place it there rather than add a second call to the array branch.

**Dev out-of-scope finding 3 — NOTED for E3 and E4.** The direct-driver answers are the measured pre-state D3's envelope replaces; nothing for E1.

**Published surface — RIGHT.** The `api-surface/data.json` delta is exactly five names, `READABLE_IDS_BRAND (const)`, `ReadableIds (const)`, `ReadableIds (interface)`, `isReadableIds (function)`, `ListComparandShapeOptions (interface)`; `export-origins/data.json` adds the four origins (`ReadableIds` keyed once, the value and the interface being one declaration-merged name in one file). The data barrel gains `export * from './readable-ids'` with an ADR-0139 comment. No `any` is exported; `ReadableIds.of` is a frozen const. No governed surface is touched (`GOVERNED_SURFACES` rows: `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`; `scripts/adr-anchors/` and `.changeset/` are on none). 703 changed lines, under the 3,000 line.

### ② Semver level

RIGHT. `.changeset/22787-readable-ids-leaf.md` declares `@objectstack/spec` `minor` and `@objectstack/objectql` `minor` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, and that is what the diff publishes: four new spec exports and one widened accept-set (a branded `$in` comparand, for the one caller that opts in), nothing removed or narrowed, and objectql's `src` moved (the wrapper now opts in and refuses). A Clause-② `yes` takes at least `minor`; both packages sit in the same fixed group in `.changeset/config.json`, so the objectql bump is consistent rather than extra. The PR body's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line matches. No ADR-0087 disposition is owed: `breakingDeclaration` in `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:645-657` reads only `major`, a BREAKING banner, a `!` summary or a `narrowing` arm, and this changeset carries none, so the gate takes its G1 branch (the dev's quoted pass line). `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation, route (admission in the spec door behind an opt-in, not in objectql's file): ANSWERED RIGHT, see ① the opt-in route.
- Deviation, no ADR-0087 marker: ANSWERED RIGHT, see ②.
- Deviation, two `scripts/adr-anchors/*.json` files outside the claim's surface: ANSWERED RIGHT. AGENTS.md Prime Directive 13 requires an implemented ADR decision to be anchored, one JSON per path, no index; `scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs` requires a non-empty `adrs`, a non-empty `invariant`, an existing file and the ADR id in that file's body, and audits each `D` letter against the record's decisions; both anchored files cite `ADR-0139` in their headers, and the invariants state real decision text, the `readable-ids` one D1's brand and fail-closed properties, the objectql one D1's single-caller admission plus the E1 interim refusal, which E2 rewrites when it composes. Not governed.
- Deviation, `@objectstack/objectql` `minor`: ANSWERED RIGHT, see ②.
- Deviation, two NOT-MEASURED gates: ANSWERED by CI. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` runs in `ci.yml`'s `build-core` job (`Build Core`, required), green on the head; `check:type-check-debt` runs in `lint.yml`'s `Type Check · debt ledger`, one of the four jobs the required `TypeScript Type Check` aggregator needs; its conclusion is in the gate line below.
- Deviation, zero label writes and one disjoint `main` commit after the last merge: NOTED, no action; the queue rebuilds on current `main`.
- Out-of-scope findings 1 and 2: ESCALATED to the E2 card under #22788 with the instruction in ①; finding 3: NOTED for E3 and E4.
- Pin gap, raised here: the `having` position is refused at the head (`engine.ts:19049` into the wrapper) but no pin asserts it, and ADR-0139 D1 names `having` as a refused position. Not a FAIL: the behaviour exists and the position cannot widen a read; E2, which moves the refusal and drops the read-verb `$in` case, must pin `having` with the other kept positions.
- Note for E2's reviewer: the activity gate's `catch` folds any filter-compute failure into `denyAll` (`activity-read-visibility.ts:138-144`); ADR-0139 D3 says a consumer does not catch the composition refusal into its deny-all sentinel. That is E5's seam, flagged now so it is not lost.

Gates on `5a4e282ffb` (check-runs read at 2026-10-11T09:20Z, not re-run): all 35 runs concluded, none red; the seven required contexts are `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` (the `debt ledger` job included), `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core` (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` included), `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Skipped, advisory and path-filtered: `Console Pin Gate`, `Build Docs`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`. `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness` and the claim and single-writer checks are `success`.
